subject: journey/ibnbattuta
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset: ONE landscape 3:2 sketchbook page, not a collage or contact sheet.
An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.

Traveller description (only this person): Ibn Battuta, a North African Moroccan scholar with warm olive-brown skin, an oval face, dark attentive eyes and a neatly kept dark beard; plain cream turban, undyed linen tunic and a muted brown wool cloak, simple leather shoes. Age twenty-one in1325, gradually older through the journey, with greying beard by1355. Keep him a modest human presence, never a generic royal portrait.

This picture: Interior viewed from a low seated guest position, Anatolian craftspeople bring fresh bread and bowls to Ibn Battuta, worn rugs and an oil lamp, Konya1332, lively natural gestures, no Ottoman fez. Historical scene in the setting of Ibn Battuta’s travels. This is an imagined journal observation, not a period artwork. Keep architecture, clothing and equipment appropriate to the fourteenth century. Vary scale and viewpoint as described; do not add an unrelated traveller portrait.
No legible text, numbers, captions, signatures or watermarks. Keep large areas of bare cream paper and loose unfinished graphite lines; avoid a polished oil painting or uniformly dense sepia rendering.
